description: XrmToolBox plugin that turns the full Power Platform Admin (PPAC) + Business Application Platform (BAP) REST surface into a searchable, executable explorer. Browse 200+ documented operations (environments, environment groups, DLP policies, billing policies, governance, capacity, lifecycle, tenant settings), execute parameter-free GETs in one click, and inspect raw JSON responses — all using the XrmToolBox connection's signed-in user via silent MSAL token exchange. Same operation catalog as the standalone VerseOps WPF app.
releaseNotes: v1.0.7 — Description tab is now a styled rich-text view instead of a plaintext dump. The HTTP method is rendered as a color-coded pill (GET green / POST blue / PUT orange / PATCH purple / DELETE red), the URL in monospace, scope in gray, then the catalog prose. For PPAC ops whose catalog description embeds "  |  Docs: <learn url>", the Microsoft Learn URL is auto-detected as a hyperlink (RichTextBox.DetectUrls) and clicking it opens the docs in the user's default browser (System.Diagnostics.Process.Start) — no WebView2 runtime, no NuGet add, no HTTP fetch, no native DLL. v1.0.6 — Fix 16 PPAC catalog token mismatches: Apply to URL + Body silently no-op'd for Copy Environment, Get Environment Copy Candidates, Get/Restore Candidates, Restore Environment, Environment Group Role Assignments (3 ops), Rule Assignments by group, and all 8 Billing Policy + Billing Policy Environment ops. Root cause: shared OpParam.Token ("environmentId" / "groupId" / "policyId") didn't match those URLs' actual placeholders ("sourceEnvironmentId" / "targetEnvironmentId" / "environmentGroupId" / "billingPolicyId"). SubstituteTokens is a literal-name regex replace and preserved the {placeholder} as-is, so clicking Apply produced a URL still containing the literal token. Added Source/Target/EnvGroup/BillingPolicy Id param variants whose Token matches the URL character-for-character. UI: param-form dropdowns now go through the same FluentStyles pass as the URL/Scope/Search controls (Segoe UI 10pt, FlatStyle.System, FixedSingle borders) instead of looking 1-2pt smaller than everything else. Cached pickers (env / group / DLP / billing) surface their cache state on the Load button caption ("Load DLP (47)") and via per-row tooltip ("Cached 47 items — type to filter"), so it's obvious the data survived an op-switch and doesn't need re-loading. v1.0.5 — Host-startup + tab-close stability. Pack Microsoft.IdentityModel.Abstractions.dll alongside MSAL: MSAL 4.81 references it transitively for its telemetry surface, and without it XrmToolBox's MEF Assembly.GetTypes() scan throws ReflectionTypeLoadException during host startup, crashing Program.Main before the tile gallery renders. Make Dispose() idempotent on the plugin control: XTB can call Dispose(true) more than once on tab close, and the second call's Cancel() on the loader/executor CancellationTokenSource was throwing ObjectDisposedException and surfacing a crash dialog. v1.0.4 — Plugin-store polish: implements IGitHubPlugin (View on GitHub button on the tile), IHelpPlugin (? button → plugin README), INoConnectionRequired (no Dataverse connection prompt — the plugin uses tenant-level MSAL, not the host's IOrganizationService). Ships a dedicated plugin-focused README so the nuget.org / plugin-store landing page no longer pitches the standalone WPF app. New ISSUE_TEMPLATE + CONTRIBUTING.md in the repo. v1.0.3 — Catalog cleanup: corrected 5 BAP routes proven 404 by tenant-side verification. "Get environment" now uses /scopes/admin/ prefix (bare path 404s for tenant-admin callers). "List backups" BAP duplicate removed (PPAC equivalent works). "Get tenant settings" switched from GET to POST {} — listTenantSettings is an ARM-style list-action verb. "Update tenant settings" /scopes/admin/ prefix dropped. "Get DLP policy" documented (URL is correct, test-rig seed mismatch). v1.0.2 — Initial XrmToolBox store release. Search executes on Enter (not per-keystroke). FluentStyles theme pass. Tile branding (32x32 + 80x80 VerseOps mark).
title: VerseOps API Explorer for Power Platform
